title: I made a dinosaur merge defense game with AI. Balancing fast and slow players has been the hard part.
author: Little-Athlete4116
selftext:
I started Dino Merge Defense because I missed the tower defense maps I played in Warcraft 3. The idea was simple enough: merge little dinosaurs, grow them up to T10 and use them to hold off waves. It's now playable on Android and iOS.



I use AI for the code and artwork. One art problem has been keeping each dinosaur recognisable across ten growth stages. A bigger version of the same picture isn't very satisfying, but changing too much makes it look like a different species. I've been working from growth-stage references and checking the results at the size they actually appear in the game.



The problem that has been much less predictable is player speed. Dinosaurs attack automatically, but the player is constantly matching pairs, clearing board space and deciding when to deploy. A stage that feels comfortable to someone who merges quickly can be rough for someone else with the same dinosaurs. The testers have been pretty blunt about that.



AI has helped me build and revise things, but deciding whether a stage feels fair still comes back to watching what players do and taking their feedback. That's where a lot of my recent difficulty changes have come from.



The screenshots show a late-chapter battle and the growth screen. Outside the campaign there are weekday bosses, spirits and a ranked arena against other players' teams. It's free to play with ads and IAP, so this is a commercial game post by its developer.



English gameplay: [https://www.youtube.com/shorts/k2JZhAq3fxc](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/k2JZhAq3fxc)

Android: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.dinomerge.defense](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.dinomerge.defense)

iOS: [https://apps.apple.com/app/id6826827925](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6826827925)



For anyone building an active merge game, how do you separate a difficulty problem from a control/readability problem when testing? That's a distinction I'm still working on.
